answer: I'd like to talk about a time technology got me out of a tricky situation abroad. A time technology genuinely saved me was when I was travelling in Nepal with two friends and struggled with a serious language barrier. It was my first proper trip abroad, so I was already slightly on edge. We had just arrived in Kathmandu late in the evening, and I found myself unable to communicate with a taxi driver, which was becoming quite [[nerve-racking]]. He spoke almost no English, and our few words of Nepali were not enough to explain where our guesthouse was. Then I remembered a translation app on my phone, which turned out to be a [[lifesaver]]. I simply typed what I wanted to say, and it translated it instantly, allowing us to understand each other. It even read the sentence out loud, and the driver laughed and nodded. It felt almost [[miraculous]] that a small device could bridge such a gap so easily. What impressed me most was how [[seamless]] and quick the whole process was. Without it, I honestly do not know how I would have managed. The experience really opened my eyes to how [[indispensable]] technology has become in daily life. While I sometimes worry that we rely on it too heavily, moments like that remind me of its genuine value. It turned a potentially frustrating situation into a smooth one, and I was extremely grateful for it. In the end we reached the guesthouse safely, and the driver even recommended a good place for breakfast. We ended up using that app for the rest of the trip.

followUps.q: Do you use translation apps in your daily life?
followUps.answer: Occasionally at work, when a student sends me a document in a language I don't know. But for English I prefer to rely on myself, because I want to keep improving my own skills.

followUps.q: Do you think technology makes travelling easier?
followUps.answer: Definitely. Maps, booking apps and translation tools remove a lot of the stress. The only downside is that people sometimes stare at their screens instead of enjoying where they are.

note: Set in Kathmandu on his trip to Nepal; plain-ish 'stressful' replaced by 'nerve-racking'; marked 'lifesaver'.
